question: Which exercise is explicitly listed among the basic control skills test exercises in the manual?
choice_a: Alley dock
choice_b: Serpentine cone weave
choice_c: Downhill hill start
choice_d: U-turn in a cul-de-sac
explanation: The manual lists straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, parallel park (driver side), parallel park (conventional), and alley dock as the basic control skills test exercises.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, This Section Covers

question: The manual lists four categories used to score the basic control skills test. Which of the following is one of them?
choice_a: Reaction time
choice_b: Pull-ups
choice_c: Fuel efficiency
choice_d: Signal timing
explanation: The manual states the examiner scores crossing boundaries (encroachments), pull-ups, outside vehicle observations (looks), and final position/inside parallel.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring

question: What is the maximum number of times you may look to check the position of your vehicle during most basic control skills exercises (other than Straight Line Backing)?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Three
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Unlimited
explanation: The manual states the maximum number of times you may look to check the position of your vehicle is two, except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows only one look.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: How many times may you look to check your vehicle's position specifically during the Straight Line Backing exercise?
choice_a: Three
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Zero
choice_d: One
explanation: The manual specifically allows only one look during the Straight Line Backing exercise, unlike the two looks allowed for other exercises.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: According to the manual, which of the following counts as a "look" during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Opening the door to check vehicle position, or walking to the back of a bus for a better view
choice_b: Checking your side mirror while backing
choice_c: Glancing at the dashboard gauges
choice_d: Asking the examiner for guidance
explanation: The manual states that each time you open the door, move from a seated position where in physical control of the vehicle, or on a bus walk to the back to get a better view, it is scored as a "look."
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: What is a "pull-up" during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Stopping without changing direction
choice_b: Stopping and pulling forward to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_c: Touching a boundary cone
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as when a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Pull-ups

question: Does the manual penalize a driver for an initial pull-up during a basic control skills exercise?
choice_a: Yes, every pull-up is scored as an automatic failure
choice_b: No, pull-ups are never counted against a driver
choice_c: No, you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number will count as errors
choice_d: Yes, but only during the Alley Dock exercise
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Pull-ups

question: What is an "encroachment" as scored on the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Backing too slowly through an exercise
choice_b: Failing to signal before backing
choice_c: Requesting an additional look
choice_d: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle, with each encroachment counting as an error.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Crossing Boundaries (Encroachments)

question: Before exiting the vehicle to check its external position (a "look"), what must you do according to the manual?
choice_a: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely
choice_c: Roll down all windows
choice_d: Notify the examiner verbally and honk the horn
explanation: The manual states that when stopping to check the external position of the vehicle, you must place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s).
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: When exiting the vehicle to take a "look," how does the manual say you must do so safely?
choice_a: Exit quickly to save time
choice_b: Face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times (or maintain a firm grasp on the handrail when exiting a bus)
choice_c: Exit from the passenger side only
choice_d: Leave the engine running and door open
explanation: The manual instructs that when exiting the vehicle, you must do so safely by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times, or maintaining a firm grasp on the handrail when exiting a bus.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: What happens if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position exactly as described by the examiner?
choice_a: Nothing, final position is not scored
choice_b: You are given unlimited extra attempts
choice_c: You will be penalized and could fail the basic skills test
choice_d: You automatically pass if you were close
explanation: The manual warns that if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, you will be penalized and could fail the basic skills test.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring, Final Position/Inside Parallel

question: What does the Straight Line Backing exercise require you to do?
choice_a: Parallel park between two vehicles without touching them
choice_b: Back into an alley within three feet of its rear boundary
choice_c: Drive forward past a space, then back into it from the right rear
choice_d: Back your vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or crossing the exercise boundaries
explanation: The manual describes Straight Line Backing as backing your vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or crossing over the exercise boundaries.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.2.1 - Straight Line Backing

question: In the Offset Back/Right exercise, after driving straight forward to the outer boundary, what must you do?
choice_a: Back the vehicle into the opposite lane until the front of your vehicle has passed the first set of cones, without striking boundary lines or cones
choice_b: Parallel park into a space on your right
choice_c: Back into an alley within three feet of the rear boundary
choice_d: Pull forward into the opposite lane
explanation: The manual states that in Offset Back/Right, from the outer boundary position you must back the vehicle into the opposite lane until the front of your vehicle has passed the first set of cones without striking boundary lines or cones.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.2.2 - Offset Back/Right

question: The Offset Back/Left exercise asks you to back into a space located where relative to your vehicle?
choice_a: Directly behind your vehicle
choice_b: To the left rear of your vehicle
choice_c: To the right rear of your vehicle
choice_d: Diagonally in front of your vehicle
explanation: The manual states that in Offset Back/Left, you may be asked to back into a space that is to the left rear of your vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.2.3 - Offset Back/Left

question: In the Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise, the parking space is located on which side of your vehicle?
choice_a: Directly behind
choice_b: The right
choice_c: The left
choice_d: Either side, examiner's choice
explanation: The manual states that in Parallel Park (Driver Side), you may be asked to park in a parallel parking space that is on your left.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.2.4 - Parallel Park (Driver Side)

question: In the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise, the parking space is located on which side of your vehicle?
choice_a: The left
choice_b: Directly ahead
choice_c: Diagonally behind
choice_d: The right
explanation: The manual states that in Parallel Park (Conventional), you may be asked to park in a parallel parking space that is on your right.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.2.5 - Parallel Park (Conventional)

question: In the Alley Dock exercise, how close must the rear of your vehicle come to the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones?
choice_a: Within three feet
choice_b: Within one foot
choice_c: Within ten feet
choice_d: Within six inches
explanation: The manual states that in Alley Dock, you must back into the alley bringing the rear of your vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 12.2.6 - Alley Dock

topic: How You Will Be Tested - General Requirements
question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following must you do at all times, according to the manual?
choice_a: Maintain exactly the posted speed limit at all times
choice_b: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Keep the radio off
choice_d: Use only the right lane regardless of traffic
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not include a certain traffic situation, what does the manual say you may be asked to do?
choice_a: Skip that portion of the test entirely
choice_b: Drive to a different route with the situation present
choice_c: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_d: Automatically receive full credit for that maneuver
explanation: The manual states that if your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate one by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing if you were in that traffic situation.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, when is coasting during a turn considered "unsafe"?
choice_a: Whenever the vehicle exceeds 10 mph
choice_b: Whenever the turn signal is not used
choice_c: Whenever the driver does not check mirrors
choice_d: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear, with the clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral, for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where does the manual say you should stop?
choice_a: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_b: As close as possible without touching the vehicle ahead
choice_c: At least three car lengths back regardless of visibility
choice_d: Wherever there is a painted stop line, even if it is far behind the vehicle ahead
explanation: The manual instructs that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you, keeping a safe gap.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: As you approach an intersection, what does the manual instruct regarding coming to a stop?
choice_a: Coast to a stop to save fuel
choice_b: Come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap
choice_c: Stop only if a pedestrian is visible
choice_d: Roll slowly through if no traffic is seen
explanation: The manual states that if necessary, you must come to a complete stop, with no coasting, behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During multiple-lane portions of the road test, what must you do before changing lanes?
choice_a: Only use turn signals, no need to check traffic
choice_b: Change lanes as quickly as possible to avoid holding up traffic
choice_c: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe
choice_d: Always change lanes to the left only
explanation: The manual states you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.4 - Lane Changes

question: What does the manual say about changing lanes or gears while any part of your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks?
choice_a: Changing gears is fine, but changing lanes is not
choice_b: Both are permitted if done smoothly
choice_c: Changing lanes is fine as long as you signal
choice_d: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing
explanation: The manual instructs that you must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: For buses, school buses, or vehicles displaying placards, within what distance range must the vehicle stop from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_c: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Exactly at the crossing gate
explanation: The manual states such vehicles should stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail, after activating the four-way flashers.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: When stopping for a student discharge, how far away from students at the stop must the school bus come to a complete stop, at minimum?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_b: At least 10 feet
choice_c: 25 feet
choice_d: 50 feet
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, where should your vehicle be positioned within the lane?
choice_a: In the left-most lane at all times
choice_b: Straddling two lanes for visibility
choice_c: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane)
choice_d: As close to the curb as possible regardless of lane markings
explanation: The manual states that during the Urban Business portion of the test, your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) while keeping up with the flow of traffic without exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.3 - Urban Business

question: After driving under an overpass during the test, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The overpass construction date
choice_b: The name of the engineering firm
choice_c: The overpass's traffic volume
choice_d: The posted clearance or height
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 13.1.9 - Bridge/Overpass/Sign
